defineUnifiedFocalLoss

Source: R/unifiedFocalLoss.R
defineUnifiedFocalLoss.Rd

Define a loss for semantic segmentation using a modified unified focal loss framework as a subclass of torch::nn_module()

Usage

defineUnifiedFocalLoss(
  nCls = 3,
  cropFactorMsk = 0,
  cropFactorPred = 0,
  lambda = 0.5,
  gamma = 0.5,
  delta = 0.6,
  smooth = 1e-08,
  zeroStart = TRUE,
  clsWghtsDist = 1,
  clsWghtsReg = 1,
  useLogCosH = FALSE,
  useEdgeDist = FALSE,
  prioritizeEdge = TRUE,
  edgeMode = "threshold",
  distThreshold = 10,
  minWght = 0.5,
  maxWght = 1,
  applyDistWght = "both",
  labelSmoothing = 0,
  classAvgDist = FALSE,
  device = "cuda"
)

Arguments

nCls

Number of classes being differentiated.

cropFactorMsk

Number of rows and columns of cells to not include for mask in assessment to minimize edge effects. Default is 0 or no cropping.

cropFactorPred

Number of rows and columns of cells to not include for prediction in assessment to minimize edge effects. Default is 0 or no cropping.

lambda

Term used to control the relative weighting of the distribution- and region-based losses. Default is 0.5, or equal weighting between the losses. If lambda = 1, only the distribution- based loss is considered. If lambda = 0, only the region-based loss is considered. Values between 0.5 and 1 put more weight on the distribution-based loss while values between 0 and 0.5 put more weight on the region-based loss.

gamma

Parameter that controls weighting applied to difficult-to-predict pixels (for distribution-based losses) or difficult-to-predict classes (for region-based losses). Smaller values increase the weight applied to difficult samples or classes. Default is 1, or no focal weighting is applied. Value must be less than or equal to 1 and larger than 0.

delta

Parameter that controls the relative weightings of false positive and false negative errors for each class. Different weightings can be provided for each class. The default is 0.6, which results in prioritizing false negative errors relative to false positive errors.

smooth

Smoothing factor to avoid divide-by-zero errors and provide numeric stability. Default is 1e-8. Recommend using the default.

zeroStart

TRUE or FALSE. If class indices start at 0 as opposed to 1, this should be set to TRUE. This is required to implement one-hot encoding since R starts indexing at 1. Default is TRUE.

clsWghtsDist

Vector of class weights for use in calculating a weighted version of the CE loss. Default is for all classes to be equally weighted.

clsWghtsReg

Vector of class weights for use in calculating a weighted version of the region-based loss. Default is for all classes to be equally weighted.

useLogCosH

TRUE or FALSE. Whether or not to apply a logCosH transformation to the region-based loss. Default is FALSE.

useEdgeDist

TRUE or FALSE. Whether to apply distance-to-class-boundary weights during loss computation. When TRUE a dist tensor must be supplied to forward. Default is FALSE.

prioritizeEdge

TRUE or FALSE. When useEdgeDist = TRUE, controls which pixels receive the higher weight. If TRUE (default), pixels near class boundaries (small distance) receive maxWght and pixels far from boundaries receive minWght. If FALSE, the weighting is reversed so that non-edge pixels are emphasised.

edgeMode

Character string specifying how the distance is converted to a per-pixel weight. One of "threshold", "linear", or "gaussian". Default is "threshold". See the Details section for a full description of each mode.

distThreshold

Numeric. The distance value (in map units or pixel units, matching the distance raster) that defines the boundary of the high-weight zone. Default is 10.

minWght

Numeric. The minimum per-pixel weight applied to loss contributions. Must be less than maxWght. Default is 0.5.

maxWght

Numeric. The maximum per-pixel weight applied to loss contributions. Must be greater than minWght. Default is 1.0.

applyDistWght

Character string controlling which loss component the edge weights are applied to. One of "distribution" (distribution-based/CE loss only), "region" (region-based/Tversky loss only), or "both" (default).

labelSmoothing

Numeric value in [0, 1). When greater than 0, this amount of probability mass is spread uniformly across all classes when computing the cross-entropy, preventing the model from becoming overconfident. The focal modifier is always derived from the true-class softmax probability gathered directly from the network output, so focal weighting is not distorted by the smoothed targets. Default is 0 (no smoothing).

classAvgDist

TRUE or FALSE. When FALSE (default), the distribution loss is computed as a pixel-level weighted mean of the focal cross-entropy, with clsWghtsDist rescaling each pixel's contribution by its true class weight. When TRUE, the focal cross-entropy is first averaged within each class and the resulting per-class means are then combined as a weighted average using clsWghtsDist. The per-class approach mirrors the macro-averaging philosophy already used by the region-based loss and can give better gradient signal to under-represented classes under severe class imbalance. Note that if a class has no pixels in a given batch its contribution is effectively zero for that step, consistent with the behaviour of the region-based loss.

device

Define device being used for computation. Define using torch_device().

Value

Loss metric for use in training process.

Details

Implementation of modified version of the unified focal loss after:

Yeung, M., Sala, E., Schönlieb, C.B. and Rundo, L., 2022. Unified focal loss: Generalising Dice and cross entropy-based losses to handle class imbalanced medical image segmentation. Computerized Medical Imaging and Graphics, 95, p.102026.

Modifications include (1) allowing users to define class weights for both the distribution- based and region-based losses, (2) using class weights as opposed to the symmetric and asymmetric methods implemented by the authors, (3) including an option to apply a logcosh transform to the region-based loss, (4) optionally incorporating distance-to-class-boundary weights computed by makeBoundaryDistance, (5) an option to compute the distribution loss as a weighted average of per-class means rather than as a single pixel-level weighted mean, and (6) optional label smoothing on the distribution loss.

This loss has three key hyperparameters that control its implementation. Lambda controls the relative weight of the distribution- and region-based losses. Default is 0.5, or equal weighting between the losses is applied. If lambda = 1, only the distribution- based loss is considered. If lambda = 0, only the region-based loss is considered. Values between 0.5 and 1 put more weight on the distribution-based loss while values between 0 and 0.5 put more weight on the region-based loss.

Gamma controls the application of focal loss and the application of increased weight to difficult-to-predict pixels (for distribution-based losses) or difficult-to-predict classes (region-based losses). Lower gamma values put increased weight on difficult samples or classes. Using a value of 1 equates to not using a focal adjustment.

The delta term controls the relative weight of false positive and false negative errors for each class. The default is 0.6 for each class, which results in placing a higher weight on false negative as opposed to false positive errors relative to that class.

By adjusting the lambda, gamma, delta, and class weight terms, the user can implement a variety of different loss metrics including cross entropy loss, weighted cross entropy loss, focal cross entropy loss, focal weighted cross entropy loss, Dice loss, focal Dice loss, Tversky loss, and focal Tversky loss.

When labelSmoothing > 0 the cross-entropy is computed against soft targets that spread labelSmoothing probability mass uniformly across all classes, reducing the model's incentive to become overconfident. The focal modifier is kept anchored to the true-class softmax probability gathered directly from the network output, so the focal weighting continues to reflect genuine model confidence rather than being distorted by the smoothed targets. Label smoothing is applied only to the distribution loss; the region-based (Tversky) loss is not affected.

When useEdgeDist = TRUE a distance-to-class-boundary tensor must be passed as the third argument to forward(pred, target, dist). The tensor should have shape (N, 1, H, W) and contain the per-pixel distances produced by makeBoundaryDistance, stacked into a batch. Pixels at a class boundary have distance 0; distance increases away from boundaries.

Three edge-weighting modes are available via edgeMode:

  • "threshold": pixels within distThreshold receive one weight; pixels beyond receive the other. When prioritizeEdge = TRUE the inside weight is maxWght and the outside weight is minWght; the relationship is reversed when prioritizeEdge = FALSE.

  • "linear": weight changes linearly from maxWght at distance 0 to minWght at distThreshold (when prioritizeEdge = TRUE), or from minWght to maxWght (when prioritizeEdge = FALSE). Beyond distThreshold the weight is clamped to the far-end value.

  • "gaussian": weight follows a Gaussian curve centred at distance 0. The curve uses sigma = distThreshold / 3 so that the weight is approximately minWght at distThreshold and falls to exactly minWght beyond it. Direction is controlled by prioritizeEdge as above.
